title: The Interior Experience of Architecture: An Emotional Connection between Space and the Body
research_focus: To provide a phenomenological understanding of interior space, exploring the emotional connection between space and experience, and identifying how interior experience can improve the quality of spatial and emotional experience through stimulating a lived body, emphasizing materiality, and generating emotional connection.

sample_context.description: Four architectural projects by prominent phenomenological architects (Peter Zumthor's Bruder Klaus Field Chapel and Serpentine Pavilion; Kengo Kuma's Sensing Space and GC Prostho Museum Research Center) were analyzed as case studies. These projects were selected for their emphasis on spatial experience, materiality, and sensory engagement.
sample_context.setting: Architectural spaces (chapel, pavilion, installation, museum) designed to evoke specific sensory and emotional experiences.

findings.antecedent: Interactive connection between the body (movements, senses) and various elements of interior space (materiality, light, sound, smell)
findings.consequent: Improved interior experience, personal connection to culture and emotion
findings.description: The body, through its movements and senses (tactility, smell, hearing, vision), continuously interacts with environmental stimuli, leading to a multi-sensory experience that forms the basis of interior perception and emotional connection. This engagement is crucial for understanding architecture beyond mere visual forms.
supporting_quotes: experiencing architecture is multi-sensory; qualities of space, matter and scale are measured together by the eye, ear, nose, skin, tongue, skeleton and muscle.
The interior space engages the body as a form to interact with.

findings.antecedent: Materiality (e.g., concrete, wood, plants, light, shadow, water, fire, aromas)
findings.consequent: Stimulated sensory effects, awareness of sensual aspects of interior space, emotional connection
findings.theme_name: Materiality as a Medium for Sensory and Emotional Connection
findings.description: Materiality acts as a medium that connects the body with interior space, directly stimulating sensory experiences (e.g., touch, smell, sight of light/shadow patterns). These sensory inputs evoke feelings and memories, enriching the spatial experience and improving its quality.
supporting_quotes: The material presence of things in a piece of architecture, its frame. That kind of things has a sensual effect on me.
materiality, as an environmental stimulus, can enhance the spatial experience by engaging the body.

findings.antecedent: Sensory effects from interior space (e.g., specific smells, textures, light patterns)
findings.consequent: Evoked personal and socially shared memories, emotional connection, cultural experience
findings.theme_name: Emotional and Cultural Connection through Memory
findings.description: Interior spaces, particularly through specific sensory stimuli like smell or light, can evoke personal and socially shared memories. These memories contribute to a sense of place, cultural identity, and emotional attachment, making the experience more profound than purely functional or visual aspects.
supporting_quotes: interior space can evoke a socially memorized spatial experience that affects one's emotions.
A particular smell... evoked a socially shared memory of a Japanese home for those visitors who had experience of living there.

findings.antecedent: Abstract spatial dimensions (e.g., darkness, filtered light, specific aromas) without traditional architectural form
findings.consequent: Spatial experience, stimulation of bodily senses, evocation of personal memory
findings.theme_name: Abstract Spatial Experience and Sensory Stimulation
findings.description: Even in abstract architectural works lacking conventional forms, specific environmental elements like darkness, filtered light, or particular aromas can stimulate bodily senses and evoke personal memories, thereby creating a rich spatial experience. This highlights the power of sensory input over purely visual or formal aspects.
supporting_quotes: abstract dimension of a work without architectural form also provides spatial experience through stimulating bodily senses and evoking personal memory.
Kuma's installation... simply provided a sense of smell in a dark room without an architectural form, but stimulated spatial experiences and emotional connections.

findings.antecedent: Integration of body, materiality, and emotion
findings.consequent: Enriched interior experience, improved quality of architecture
findings.theme_name: Integrated Understanding for Quality Interior Experience
findings.description: An integrated understanding of how the body interacts with materiality and how these interactions generate emotions is fundamental to enriching the interior experience. This holistic approach, encompassing physical, sensory, cultural, and mental aspects, is key to improving the overall quality of architecture.
supporting_quotes: an integrated understanding of the body, materiality (environmental stimuli), and how emotion plays a substantial role in improving the quality of the interior experience.
The body, materiality, and emotional connection offer a fundamental idea for enriching the interior experience.

themes_or_constructs: Materiality as a Medium for Sensory and Emotional Connection
Emotional and Cultural Connection through Memory
Abstract Spatial Experience and Sensory Stimulation
Integrated Understanding for Quality Interior Experience
supporting_quotes_or_evidence_snippets: experiencing architecture is multi-sensory; qualities of space, matter and scale are measured together by the eye, ear, nose, skin, tongue, skeleton and muscle.
The material presence of things in a piece of architecture, its frame. That kind of things has a sensual effect on me.
interior space can evoke a socially memorized spatial experience that affects one's emotions.
A particular smell... which was left behind in Bruder Klaus Field Chapel, can directly link that place with something that was burned in the past.
Kuma's installation... simply provided a sense of smell in a dark room without an architectural form, but stimulated spatial experiences and emotional connections.
The interior space engages the body as a form to interact with.
The interior space can be transformed into a place through bodily experience.
derived_hypotheses: An interactive connection between the body and various elements of interior space improves the interior experience, providing a personal connection to culture and emotion.

Sensory effects that enhance the emotional connection with the interior space can potentially enrich the spatial experience and improve its quality to greater effect than functional or form-oriented factors.
mechanism_candidates: Multi-sensory stimulation (tactile, olfactory, auditory, visual) through materiality and environmental elements.
Phenomenological engagement of the lived body with space.
Evocation of personal and socially shared memories through sensory cues.
Construction of affect and meaning through interoceptive processing and environmental interaction.
Cultural conditioning of sensory perception and emotional responses to specific environmental stimuli.
transferability_limits: The findings are based on a limited number of case studies (four architectural projects), which may restrict generalizability to other architectural environments.
The interpretation and analysis of data reflect the researcher's perspectives, potentially introducing subjective views.
limitations: Only four case studies were explored, limiting the generalizability of findings to diverse architectural environments.
The data were interpreted and analyzed by reflecting the researcher's perspectives, which could provide a subjective view in some respects.

paper_metadata.title: The Interior Experience of Architecture: An Emotional Connection between Space and the Body
paper_metadata.crossref_title: The Interior Experience of Architecture: An Emotional Connection between Space and the Body
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: This paper provides a phenomenological understanding of interior space to explore the emotional connection between space and experience. It focuses on the significant aspects of interior space, considering how people experience interior space and which aspects improve the quality of spatial and emotional experience. I have argued that the interior experience offers effective ways of stimulating emotional experience to create spatial perception as a way of understanding architecture. Interior experience can be developed through: (a) stimulating a lived body; (b) emphasizing materiality; and (c) generating emotional connection. This allows people to develop an awareness of the sensual aspects of the interior space and improve the quality of their emotional experiences. I have drawn upon representative case studies about spatial experience to explore how they use materiality to stimulate sensory effects and how the multi-sensory space connects with emotional experience, which is one of the fundamental aspects of this paper. I found that an integrated body and materiality are fundamental elements that are needed to enrich the spatial experience, even in an abstract dimension of the work without architectural form. Thus, this paper contributes to the understanding and knowledge of the relationship between interior space and experience with respect to improving the quality of the emotional experience in order to develop spatial experience and considering how experience intervenes in interior space to create a multi-sensory space.
